# Performance

## Conditions

- Images on local storage, in the page cache; output to local disk.
- One run at a time, under a lock; tools alternated.
- **Each figure is the mean of 3 runs** (FLAC figures: 2 runs).
- `sacd_extract` was a generic x86-64 build. pysacd was built native
  (`-march=native`) and portable; they gave the same results for DSF output.

A single benchmark is never the whole story. Measure on your own discs.

## Extracting to DSF

Wall-clock seconds, with CPU seconds in brackets:

| | 16-core/32-thread Ryzen AI Max+ 395<br>`sacd_extract` | <br>pysacd | 10-core/12-thread Core i5-1235U<br>`sacd_extract` | <br>pysacd |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Plain DSD, stereo (78 min) | 3.2 (2.9) | **1.3** (2.0) | 7.9 (6.0) | **2.2** (4.7) |
| DST, stereo (50 min) | 7.9 (245) | 7.8 (243) | 42.0 (457) | 39.7 (451) |
| DST, stereo + 5.1 | 35.6 (1094) | 33.4 (1020) | 175.2 (1958) | 159.3 (1817) |

- **Plain DSD** is where the single-pass engine shows: 2.5× and 3.6× faster.
- **DST** decoding costs about 500 CPU-seconds per disc in either tool, and
  both spread it over every core. pysacd was level to 9% faster when this table was
  measured; since the faster decoder (#78) it is 2.4–2.6× faster than `sacd_extract` on
  DST discs (see [DST decoder speed](#dst-decoder-speed)).

## Thread scaling

DST stereo + 5.1 on the 16-core machine:

| Threads | 1 | 8 | 16 | 32 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wall | 515 s | 68.6 s (7.5×) | 40.3 s (12.8×) | 33.9 s |

Hyper-threading adds 16–19%.

## DST decoder speed

The arithmetic decoder's renormalisation is branch-free (#21): whether it's needed depends on
the data, so the branch mispredicted often. Same 16-core machine, mean of 3 alternating runs,
output byte-identical:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| DST stereo to DSF, all threads | 6.87 s (211 CPU-s) | **6.29 s** (190 CPU-s) |
| DST 5.1 to DSF, all threads | 19.01 s (587 CPU-s) | **18.25 s** (561 CPU-s) |
| one thread, stereo | 0.537 ms/frame | **0.410 ms/frame** |
| one thread, 6 channels | 1.26 ms/frame | **1.15 ms/frame** |

The tables above predate this change.

### Per-byte prediction and a code-bit window (#78)

Most of the time went into the prediction filter: 16 table lookups per bit and channel,
plus a 128-bit shift register to update. The taps on all but the 8 newest bits only see
bytes that are already decoded, so they are now computed once per output byte, for its 8
bits at once, from vector tables (16 lookups and vector adds per byte instead of 128).
The arithmetic decoder keeps its code value in a 64-bit window of code bits, so
renormalising is one shift. Output is byte-identical: the test suite, a differential test
of the old and new decoders on 60,000 mutated real frames (including the corrupt-stream
paths), and the SHA-256 of every DSF file from real DST discs.

One thread, decoding only (the frames of 4 stretches of a real disc, in memory; mean of 3
alternating runs under the benchmark lock):

| ms/frame | 16-core Ryzen AI Max+ 395<br>before | <br>after | 10-core Core i5-1235U, P-core<br>before | <br>after | E-core<br>before | <br>after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stereo | 0.410 | **0.225** (1.82×) | 1.19 | **0.74** (1.60×) | 1.36 | **0.78** (1.75×) |
| 6 channels | 1.152 | **0.670** (1.72×) | 3.02 | **2.09** (1.44×) | 4.27 | **2.29** (1.86×) |
| 5 channels (another disc) | 0.964 | **0.533** (1.81×) | | | | |

End to end, DST disc to DSF on every thread of the 10-core machine (`-s`, 12 threads; image
copied into the container, output in `/dev/shm`; mean of 3 runs, tools alternated; every
DSF file identical across the three tools):

| Wall s (CPU s) | `sacd_extract` | pysacd before | pysacd after |
|---|---|---|---|
| DST stereo (50 min) | 43.4 (467) | 33.9 (370) | **19.5** (210): 2.2× `sacd_extract` |
| DST stereo + 5.1 | 181.8 (1989) | 137.2 (1525) | **78.8** (837): 2.3× `sacd_extract` |

DSF and DSDIFF outputs also no longer decode the context frames that each batch of 32
carries for the PCM filters (2 before, 1 after), which saved 3 decodes in 35:

| Wall s (CPU s), 10-core machine as above | `sacd_extract` | pysacd, faster decoder | + core frames only |
|---|---|---|---|
| DST stereo | 43.4 (467) | 19.5 (210) | **18.0** (193): 2.4× `sacd_extract` |
| DST stereo + 5.1 | 181.8 (1989) | 78.8 (837) | **69.5** (758): 2.6× `sacd_extract` |

On one core of the 16-core machine (every process pinned to one CPU, `--threads 1`; DST
stereo to DSF, mean of 3 alternating runs, identical files): `sacd_extract` 154.7 s, pysacd
before #78 102.2 s, after both changes **51.6 s** (3.0× `sacd_extract`).

Tried and dropped (single thread, 16-core machine unless stated):

- SIMD dot products of the history with the coefficients instead of tables: 0.366 ms/frame
  stereo, against 0.273 for the first table version.
- 4-bit tables (8 KB per filter instead of 64 KB, to stay in L1): slower everywhere,
  including the i5's E-cores (0.83 against 0.78 ms/frame stereo).
- Working out the next bit's probability for both values of the current bit: fewer
  dependent steps, but more instructions; 0.258 against 0.225.
- Computing both renormalisation shifts while the comparison is pending (conditional
  moves through inline assembly, since GCC turns the C form into a branch): −1% on
  6 channels, +6% on stereo.
- A multiplication table for the interval split: 0.256 against 0.237.
- Computing the far taps a byte ahead: no change.

## FLAC instead of DSF

`pysacd convert` on the 16-core machine (`sacd_extract` has no FLAC output).
The only extra work is DSD→PCM conversion and FLAC encoding, which takes about
37 CPU-seconds per disc:

| | DSF | FLAC 24/88.2 |
|---|---|---|
| Plain DSD, stereo | 1.2 s (1.7) | 4.6 s (37.6) |
| DST, stereo | 8.0 s (239) | 10.0 s (277) |

- **On a DST disc**, FLAC adds about 14% CPU on top of the decode.
- **Portable builds** (`make PORTABLE=1`, and future wheels) pick the PCM
  filter's code at load time for the CPU: AVX-512, AVX2+FMA or the SSE2
  baseline. On the 16-core machine, converting 6 channels takes 0.29 s per
  2,000 frames, against 0.25 s for a native build and 0.41 s for a portable
  build without dispatch (mean of 5 runs).

## Hardening

The engine is built with hardening flags on Linux (see [development](development.md#building)):
`_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3`, the strong stack protector, stack-clash protection, CET, full RELRO and
a non-executable stack. Measured against `HARDEN=0` on the 16-core machine, alternating builds,
mean of 3 runs:

| Case | Build | `HARDEN=0` | `HARDEN=1` | CPU time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| plain DSD → DSF (stereo) | native | 1.15 s | 1.11 s | ±0 (1.8 → 1.7 s) |
| | portable | 1.12 s | 1.10 s | ±0 |
| DST → DSF (stereo) | native | 6.69 s | 6.56 s | +0.5% |
| | portable | 7.43 s | 7.65 s | +0.4% |
| DST → FLAC (`pysacd convert`) | native | 8.58 s | 8.88 s | +0.5% |
| | portable | 9.81 s | 9.77 s | +1.1% |

CPU time rises by at most about 1%. The wall-time differences, from −3.5% to +3.5%, go both
ways and are within run-to-run variation.

## Reading a TOC: in-process against a subprocess

A DST disc, 200 reads × 3 rounds, median:

| | Time per disc |
|---|---|
| `pysacd.read_toc()`, in-process | **0.28 ms** |
| spawning `sacd_extract -P` and capturing its text | 1.13 ms, before parsing it |

The time saved is small next to what you get: a structured object, not text
to parse.
